verdict.rationale: Sentry's own marketing describes Seer, a debugging agent that 'fixes what's broken while you ship what's next' by generating merge-ready patches. That implies autonomous background work, and Sentry also maps incidents to releases, PRs, and owners automatically. However, there is no evidence that users can configure, trigger, or schedule their own automations; the agent-tracing docs only cover monitoring of agents. Missing for 10: documentation of user-configurable automation setup, triggers or recurring schedules for background runs, controls over autonomous actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Fixes what’s broken while you ship what’s next – generating precise, merge-ready patches.
Find root causes and fix production issues with [Seer, our debugging agent]
Map every incident to the release, PR, and owner -- automatically.
